units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
मायाकल्पितमातृतामुखमृषाद्वैतप्रपञ्चाश्रयः
सत्यज्ञानसुखात्मकः श्रुतिशिखोत्थाखण्डधीगोचरः ।
मिथ्याबन्धविधूननेन परमानन्दैकरतानात्मकं
मोक्षं प्राप्त इव स्वयं विजयते विष्णुर्विकल्पोज्झितः ॥1॥
units.translation: Free from conceptual divisions, Viṣṇu himself shines forth as though he had attained liberation. That liberation is a single, unbroken fullness of supreme bliss, reached by the removal of false bondage. He is the ground of the false duality-world projected by Māyā, beginning with the apparent knower; his nature is reality, consciousness, and bliss, and he is known by the undivided understanding arising from the Upaniṣads.

gloss.en: projected by Māyā
beginning with the apparent knower
the ground of the false duality-world
whose nature is reality, consciousness, and bliss
arising from the crest of the Upaniṣads
known by undivided understanding
by the removal of false bondage
whose nature is an unbroken fullness of supreme bliss
as though having attained liberation
shines forth of his own accord
Viṣṇu, free from conceptual divisions

units.iast:
māyākalpitamātṛtāmukhamṛṣādvaitaprapañcāśrayaḥ
satyajñānasukhātmakaḥ śrutiśikhotthākhaṇḍadhīgocaraḥ |
mithyābandhavidhūnanena paramānandaikaratānātmakaṃ
mokṣaṃ prāpta iva svayaṃ vijayate viṣṇurvikalpojjhitaḥ ||1||

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
श्रीरामविश्वेश्वरमाधवानामैक्येन साक्षात्कृतमाधवानाम् ।
स्पर्शेन निर्धूततमोरजोभ्यः पादोत्थितेभ्योऽस्तु नमो रजोभ्यः ॥2॥
units.translation: Homage be to the particles of dust risen from the feet of Śrī Rāma, Viśveśvara, and Mādhava, who directly realized Mādhava through unity, and by contact with which darkness and passion are swept away.

gloss.en: of Śrī Rāma, Viśveśvara, and Mādhava
through unity
of those who directly realized Mādhava
by contact
by which darkness and passion are driven away
to the particles of dust risen from the feet
may there be homage

units.iast:
śrīrāmaviśveśvaramādhavānāmaikyena sākṣātkṛtamādhavānām |
sparśena nirdhūtatamorajobhyaḥ pādotthitebhyo’stu namo rajobhyaḥ ||2||

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
बहुभिर्विहिता बुधैः परार्थं विजयन्तेऽमितविस्तृता निबन्धाः ।
मम तु श्रम एष नूनमात्मम्भरितां भावयितुं भविष्यतीह ॥3॥
units.translation: Many treatises of immeasurable scope, composed by the wise for the benefit of others, flourish. But this effort of mine here will surely serve only for my own satisfaction.

gloss.en: composed by many
by the wise
for the benefit of others
flourish
treatises of immeasurable scope
but as for me
this effort
surely
to provide for my own satisfaction
will be here

units.iast:
bahubhirvihitā budhaiḥ parārthaṃ vijayante’mitavistṛtā nibandhāḥ |
mama tu śrama eṣa nūnamātmambharitāṃ bhāvayituṃ bhaviṣyatīha ||3||

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
श्रद्धाधनेन मुनिना मधुसूदनेन सङ्गृह्य शास्त्रनिचयं रचितातियत्नात् ।
बोधाय वादिविजयाय च सत्वराणामद्वैतसिद्धिरियमस्तु मुदे बुधानाम् ॥4॥
units.translation: May this Advaita Siddhi, composed with great effort by the sage Madhusūdana, rich in faith, after gathering the body of scripture, bring delight to the wise who are eager for understanding and victory in debate.

gloss.en: rich in faith
by the sage Madhusūdana
having gathered
the body of scripture
composed with great effort
for understanding
and for victory in debate
of those who are eager
may this Advaita Siddhi be
for the delight of the wise

śraddhādhanena muninā madhusūdanena saṅgṛhya śāstranicayaṃ racitātiyatnāt |
bodhāya vādivijayāya ca satvarāṇāmadvaitasiddhiriyamastu mude budhānām ||4||

units.label: Prose passage
units.deva:
तत्राद्वैतसिद्धेर्द्वैतमिथ्यात्वसिद्धिपूर्वकत्वाद् द्वैतमिथ्यात्वमेव प्रथममुपपादनीयम्। उपपादनं च स्वपक्षसाधनपरपक्षनिराकरणाभ्यां भवतीति तदुभयं वादजल्पवितण्डानामन्यतमां कथामाश्रित्य सम्पादनीयम्। तत्र च विप्रतिपत्तिजन्यसंशयस्य विचाराङ्गत्वान्मध्यस्थेनादौ विप्रतिपत्तिः प्रदर्शनीया। यद्यपि विप्रतिपत्तिजन्यसंशयस्य न पक्षतासम्पादकतयोपयोगः, सिषाधयिषाविरहसहकृतसाधकमानाभावरूपायास्तस्याः संशयाघटितत्वात्। अन्यथा श्रुत्याऽऽत्मनिश्चयवतोऽनुमित्सया तदनुमानं न स्यात्। वाद्यादीनां निश्चयवत्त्वेन संशयासम्भवा दाहार्यसंशयस्यातिप्रसञ्जकत्वाच्च। नापि विप्रतिपत्तेः स्वरूपत एव पक्षप्रतिपक्षपरिग्रहफलतयोपयोगः। “त्वयेदं साधनीयम्” “अनेनेदं दूषणीयम्” इत्यादिमध्यस्थवाक्यादेव तल्लाभेन विप्रतिपत्तिवैयर्थ्यात्। तथापि विप्रतिप्रत्तिजन्यसंशयस्यानुमित्यनङ्गत्वेऽपि व्युदसनीयतया विचाराङ्गत्वमस्त्येव। तादृशसंशयं प्रति विप्रतिपत्तेः क्वचिन्निश्चयादिना प्रतिबन्धादजनकत्वेऽपि स्वरूपयोग्यत्वात्। वाद्यादीनां च निश्चयवत्त्वे नियमाभावात्। “निश्चितौ हि वादं कुरुतः” इत्याभिमानिकनिश्चयाभिप्रायम्। परपक्षमालम्ब्याप्यहङ्कारिणो विपरीतनिश्चयवतो जल्पादौ प्रवृत्तिदर्शनात्। तस्मात् समयबन्धादिवत् स्वकर्तव्यनिर्वाहाय मध्यस्थेन विप्रतिपत्तिः प्रदर्शनीयैव।

तत्र मिथ्यात्वे विप्रतिपत्तिः—ब्रह्मप्रमातिरिक्ताबाध्यत्वे सति सत्त्वेन प्रतीत्यर्हं चिद्भिन्नं प्रतिपन्नोपाधौ त्रैकालिकनिषेधप्रतियोगि न वा? पारमार्थिकत्वाकारेणोक्तनिषेधप्रतियोगि न वेति। अत्र च पक्षतावच्छेदकसामानाधिकरण्येन साध्यसिद्धेरुद्देश्यत्वात् पक्षैकदेशे साध्यसिद्धावपि सिद्धसाधनतेति मते शुक्तिरूप्ये सिद्धसाधनवारणाय ब्रह्मज्ञानेतराबाध्यत्वं पक्षविशेषणम्। यदि पुनः पक्षतावच्छेदकावच्छेदेनैव साध्यसिद्धिरुद्देश्या तदैकदेशे साध्यसिद्धावपि सिद्धसाधनाभावात् तद्वारकं विशेषणमनुपादेयम्। इतरविशेषणद्वयं तु तुच्छे ब्रह्मणि च बाधवारणायादरणीयमेव। प्रत्येकं वा विप्रतिपत्तिः—वियन्मिथ्या न वा? पृथिवी मिथ्या न वेति। एवं वियदादेः प्रत्येकं पक्षत्वेऽपि न घटादौ सन्दिग्धानैकान्तिकता। पक्षसमत्वाद् घटादेः। तथा हि—पक्षे साध्याभावसन्देहस्यानुगुणत्वात् पक्षभिन्न एव तस्य दूषणत्वं वाच्यम्। अत एवोक्तं “साध्याभावनिश्चयवति हेतुसन्देहे एव सन्दिग्धानैकान्तिकता” इति। पक्षत्वं तु साध्यसन्देहवत्त्वम्। साध्यगोचरसाधकमानाभाववत्त्वं वा। एतच्च घटादिसाधारणम्। अत एव तत्रापि सन्दिग्धानैकान्तिकत्वं न दोषः। पक्षसमत्वोक्तिस्तु प्रतिज्ञाविषयत्वाभावमात्रेण। न च तर्हि प्रतिज्ञाविषयत्वमेव पक्षत्वम्। स्वार्थानुमाने तदभावात्.
units.translation:
Since the establishment of non-duality depends on first establishing that duality is false, the falsity of duality itself must first be proved. Proof consists in establishing one’s own position and refuting the opponent’s; both tasks are to be carried out through one of the forms of philosophical discussion: truth-seeking debate, contentious dispute, or refutation-only disputation. Because doubt arising from disagreement is part of inquiry, the impartial moderator must first state the disagreement.

Although doubt arising from disagreement does not help produce the status of a proposition as the subject of inference, that status is defined as the absence of a proof-producing means of knowledge together with the absence of a wish to establish the point; it does not include doubt. Otherwise, someone certain of the Self through scripture could not infer it while wishing to do so. Nor is doubt possible because debaters and others are certain; moreover, assuming a merely imagined doubt would lead to too many cases. Disagreement also does not help in itself by producing the acceptance of a thesis and its counter-thesis: the moderator’s words—“You must prove this” and “This must be refuted by the other”—already accomplish that, so disagreement would be pointless. Still, although doubt generated by disagreement is not a part of inference, it is a part of inquiry because it must be removed. Even if disagreement sometimes fails to produce such doubt because it is blocked by certainty or the like, it is naturally capable of producing it; and there is no rule that debaters and the rest must be certain. The statement “For the two who are certain conduct a debate” refers to a certainty they presume for themselves. We see that arrogant people, even while adopting the opponent’s side and holding a mistaken certainty, engage in disputation and the like. Therefore, as with establishing the terms of a debate, the impartial moderator must indeed state the disagreement to fulfill the task incumbent on him.

The disagreement concerning falsity is stated as follows: Is what is distinct from consciousness, fit to be apprehended as existent while not sublatable by any cognition other than knowledge of Brahman, and the counterpositive of a negation at all three times in the locus where it is presented—or is it not? Or, under the aspect of ultimate reality, is it the counterpositive of that stated negation, or is it not? Here the aim is to establish the predicate in the same locus as the delimiting condition of the subject. According to the view that establishing the predicate even for one part of the subject would make the proof redundant, the subject is qualified as “not sublated by anything other than knowledge of Brahman,” to avoid redundant proof in the shell-and-silver case. If, however, one intends to establish the predicate exactly within the delimitation of the subject, then proving it for only part of the subject does not make the proof redundant, and the qualifier that prevents this need not be included. The remaining two qualifications must still be retained to avoid a contradiction concerning sheer nonbeing and Brahman.

Alternatively, the disagreement may be stated separately: Is space false or not? Is earth false or not? Even when space and the other elements are each taken as the subject, a pot and the like do not give rise to doubt-based inconclusiveness, because a pot is on a par with the subject. Doubt about the absence of the predicate in the subject supports the inference; it is a defect only in something other than the subject. Hence the statement: “A doubtful reason is a doubt-based fallacy of inconclusiveness only where the absence of the predicate is certain.” Subjecthood is having doubt about the predicate, or lacking a valid means of knowledge that establishes it; this condition also applies to pots and the like. For that reason, doubt-based inconclusiveness is no defect there either. Saying that a pot is on a par with the subject means only that it is not the object of the proposition. But then is being the object of the proposition itself what makes something the subject? No, because that is absent in inference for oneself.

tatrādvaitasiddherdvaitamithyātvasiddhipūrvakatvād dvaitamithyātvameva prathamamupapādanīyam| upapādanaṃ ca svapakṣasādhanaparapakṣanirākaraṇābhyāṃ bhavatīti tadubhayaṃ vādajalpavitaṇḍānāmanyatamāṃ kathāmāśritya sampādanīyam| tatra ca vipratipattijanyasaṃśayasya vicārāṅgatvānmadhyasthenādau vipratipattiḥ pradarśanīyā| yadyapi vipratipattijanyasaṃśayasya na pakṣatāsampādakatayopayogaḥ, siṣādhayiṣāvirahasahakṛtasādhakamānābhāvarūpāyāstasyāḥ saṃśayāghaṭitatvāt| anyathā śrutyā’’tmaniścayavato’numitsayā tadanumānaṃ na syāt| vādyādīnāṃ niścayavattvena saṃśayāsambhavā dāhāryasaṃśayasyātiprasañjakatvācca| nāpi vipratipatteḥ svarūpata eva pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahaphalatayopayogaḥ| “tvayedaṃ sādhanīyam” “anenedaṃ dūṣaṇīyam” ityādimadhyasthavākyādeva tallābhena vipratipattivaiyarthyāt| tathāpi vipratiprattijanyasaṃśayasyānumityanaṅgatve’pi vyudasanīyatayā vicārāṅgatvamastyeva| tādṛśasaṃśayaṃ prati vipratipatteḥ kvacinniścayādinā pratibandhādajanakatve’pi svarūpayogyatvāt| vādyādīnāṃ ca niścayavattve niyamābhāvāt| “niścitau hi vādaṃ kurutaḥ” ityābhimānikaniścayābhiprāyam| parapakṣamālambyāpyahaṅkāriṇo viparītaniścayavato jalpādau pravṛttidarśanāt| tasmāt samayabandhādivat svakartavyanirvāhāya madhyasthena vipratipattiḥ pradarśanīyaiva|

tatra mithyātve vipratipattiḥ—brahmapramātiriktābādhyatve sati sattvena pratītyarhaṃ cidbhinnaṃ pratipannopādhau traikālikaniṣedhapratiyogi na vā? pāramārthikatvākāreṇoktaniṣedhapratiyogi na veti| atra ca pakṣatāvacchedakasāmānādhikaraṇyena sādhyasiddheruddeśyatvāt pakṣaikadeśe sādhyasiddhāvapi siddhasādhanateti mate śuktirūpye siddhasādhanavāraṇāya brahmajñānetarābādhyatvaṃ pakṣaviśeṣaṇam| yadi punaḥ pakṣatāvacchedakāvacchedenaiva sādhyasiddhiruddeśyā tadaikadeśe sādhyasiddhāvapi siddhasādhanābhāvāt tadvārakaṃ viśeṣaṇamanupādeyam| itaraviśeṣaṇadvayaṃ tu tucche brahmaṇi ca bādhavāraṇāyādaraṇīyameva| pratyekaṃ vā vipratipattiḥ—viyanmithyā na vā? pṛthivī mithyā na veti| evaṃ viyadādeḥ pratyekaṃ pakṣatve’pi na ghaṭādau sandigdhānaikāntikatā| pakṣasamatvād ghaṭādeḥ| tathā hi—pakṣe sādhyābhāvasandehasyānuguṇatvāt pakṣabhinna eva tasya dūṣaṇatvaṃ vācyam| ata evoktaṃ “sādhyābhāvaniścayavati hetusandehe eva sandigdhānaikāntikatā” iti| pakṣatvaṃ tu sādhyasandehavattvam| sādhyagocarasādhakamānābhāvavattvaṃ vā| etacca ghaṭādisādhāraṇam| ata eva tatrāpi sandigdhānaikāntikatvaṃ na doṣaḥ| pakṣasamatvoktistu pratijñāviṣayatvābhāvamātreṇa| na ca tarhi pratijñāviṣayatvameva pakṣatvam| svārthānumāne tadabhāvāt.

units.label: Prose passage
units.sectionTitle: 3. Earlier inferences for falsity · मिथ्यात्वे परोक्तानुमानानि
units.deva:
एवं विप्रतिपत्तौ प्राचां प्रयोगाः—विमतं मिथ्या दृश्यत्वात्, जडत्वात्, परिच्छिन्नत्वात्, शुक्तिरूप्यवदिति। नावयवेष्वाग्रहः। अत्र स्वनियामकनियतया विप्रतिपत्त्या लघुभूतया पक्षतावच्छेदो न विरुद्धः। समयबन्धादिना व्यवधानात्। तस्य अनुमानकालासत्त्वेऽपि उपलक्षणतया पक्षतावच्छेदकत्वम्।

यद्वा विप्रतिपत्तिविषयतावच्छेदकमेव पक्षतावच्छेदकम्। प्राचां प्रयोगेष्वपि विमतमिति पदं विप्रतिपत्तिविषयतावच्छेदकावच्छिन्नाभिप्रायेणेत्यदोषः।
units.iast:
evaṃ vipratipattau prācāṃ prayogāḥ—vimataṃ mithyā dṛśyatvāt, jaḍatvāt, paricchinnatvāt, śuktirūpyavaditi| nāvayaveṣvāgrahaḥ| atra svaniyāmakaniyatayā vipratipattyā laghubhūtayā pakṣatāvacchedo na viruddhaḥ| samayabandhādinā vyavadhānāt| tasya anumānakālāsattve’pi upalakṣaṇatayā pakṣatāvacchedakatvam|

yadvā vipratipattiviṣayatāvacchedakameva pakṣatāvacchedakam| prācāṃ prayogeṣvapi vimatamiti padaṃ vipratipattiviṣayatāvacchedakāvacchinnābhiprāyeṇetyadoṣaḥ|
units.translation:
The earlier formulation in this context of disagreement is: “The disputed object is false because it is perceptible, inert, limited, and like shell-silver.” There is no insistence on every member of the inference. Here it is not improper to delimit the subject by a concise statement of disagreement, restricted by its own governing condition, because an agreement and the like intervene. Although it is absent at the time of inference, it still delimits the subject by way of an indicator.

Or the delimitor of the subject is precisely the delimitor of the object of the disagreement. Even in the earlier formulation, the word “disputed” is intended to mean what is delimited by the delimitor of the object of disagreement; therefore there is no defect.
